title: Current of Electricity
seo_title: Secondary 4 Physics: Current of Electricity Worksheets (O-Level 6091 with Answers)
standard_text: State that current is a rate of flow of charge and recall and apply Q = It; distinguish between conventional current and electron flow; define electromotive force and potential difference as work done per unit charge and apply V = W ÷ Q; describe how to measure current and potential difference with ammeters and voltmeters; define resistance and apply R = V ÷ I; recall and apply R = ρL ÷ A; sketch and interpret the I-V characteristics of a metallic conductor at constant temperature, a filament lamp and a semiconductor diode (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Physics 6091 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 4 O-Level Physics worksheets on current of electricity: charge and current (Q = It), e.m.f. and potential difference, resistance, resistivity and I-V graphs. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Q = It, V = W ÷ Q, R = V ÷ I
key_sub: R = ρL ÷ A: longer wire, more resistance; thicker wire, less.
body_html:
How to think about it

Current is the rate of flow of charge.

  • Q = It (coulombs = amperes × seconds). Conventional current flows from + to −; electrons flow from − to +.
  • E.m.f. and p.d. are work done per unit charge: V = W ÷ Q (1 V = 1 J/C).
  • Resistance R = V ÷ I (ohms). For a wire R = ρL ÷ A, where ρ is the resistivity (Ω m).
  • I-V graphs: resistor at constant temperature is a straight line through the origin; a filament lamp curves (R rises when hot); a diode conducts one way only.
Example

3 A flows for 2 min. Charge?

t = 120 s

Q = 3 × 120

Answer: 360 C

Example

6 V across a resistor, 0.3 A through it. Resistance?

R = 6 ÷ 0.3

Answer: 20 Ω

Common mistakes

  • Thinking current is used up in a lamp.
  • Writing R = I ÷ V.
  • Forgetting to change minutes into seconds or mA into A.
  • Thinking a thicker wire has more resistance. It has less (larger area).

faq.q: What is the difference between e.m.f. and potential difference?
faq.a: E.m.f. is the energy per unit charge supplied by a source to drive charge round the whole circuit; p.d. is the energy per unit charge transferred in one component.

faq.q: How does the length and thickness of a wire affect its resistance?
faq.a: Resistance is proportional to length and inversely proportional to cross-sectional area: R = ρL ÷ A.

faq.q: Why is the I-V graph of a filament lamp curved?
faq.a: As the current rises the filament gets hotter, its resistance increases, so the current rises less for each extra volt.

items.q: What does the I–V graph for a filament lamp look like?

A curve: resistance increases as the filament gets hotter.
